Integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/*.rs and use common::call_tool_raw and NamedTempFile. conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity (ci.yml lines 135-137); workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used (test exemptions via cfg_attr) and undocumented_unsafe_blocks; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans (ci.yml line 211); REUSE compliance with SPDX headers.
conventions.error_handling: Language handlers never panic: they return Option or Vec<String>, use bounds-checked get_node_text or source slices guarded by end_byte() <= source.len(), and return Vec::new() for wrong node kinds (swift.rs line 50-52). Query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError (parser.rs 159-165). unwrap and expect appear only in tests.

patterns: Registry pattern: a new language touches languages/mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info arm, get_ts_language arm) and lang.rs (EXTENSION_MAP tuple, supported_languages slice). Verified against the swift and css wiring.

LanguageInfo field population: Java sets extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type; css and yaml set every optional to None except the queries they use. The issue excludes the three find_* handlers, so PHP sets them to None.

Java ELEMENT_QUERY (verbatim, java.rs line 4): "(method_declaration
  name: (identifier) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (identifier) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (identifier) @interface_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (identifier) @enum_name) @class
"

Java DEFUSE_QUERY (verbatim, java.rs line 32): "(local_variable_declaration declarator: (variable_declarator name: (identifier) @write.local))
(assignment_expression left: (identifier) @write.assign)
(update_expression (identifier) @writeread.update)
(identifier) @read.usage
"

Java CALL_QUERY (verbatim): "(method_invocation\n  name: (identifier) @call)"; Java IMPORT_QUERY (verbatim): "(import_declaration) @import_path"; Java REFERENCE_QUERY (verbatim): "(type_identifier) @type_ref".

Java extract_inheritance reads child_by_field_name("superclass") and child_by_field_name("interfaces") and emits "extends X" and "implements X" from type_identifier children. PHP has no such fields, so the Java walk cannot be copied as-is.

Swift extract_inheritance (swift.rs 49-75) guards on node.kind() != "class_declaration", iterates node.child(i) for kind "inheritance_specifier", and emits "extends" for the first base and "conforms" for the rest. Its no-inheritance test is a stack walk that asserts is_empty().

The tree-sitter-php upstream tags.scm (queries/tags.scm) already uses name: (name) for definitions, (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) for implements, and (function_call_expression function: ...), (scoped_call_expression name: (name)), (member_call_expression name: (name)) for calls. These are a verified template for the PHP queries.
CSS pattern: a query-only handler with ELEMENT_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, an empty CALL_QUERY ("") and no defuse; css.rs tests use a parse_and_query helper that returns capture text.

Java and Swift both wrap the query-compiled capture logic in parser_elements.rs; only the capture names function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name and type_name affect element output, so PHP interface_name, trait_name and enum_name fall back to child_by_field_name("name").

constraints: LanguageInfo.defuse_query is Option<&'static str>; a None value disables def-use for the language (parser_elements.rs 850 returns early). The issue's scope lists DEFUSE_QUERY as required.
Query text is compiled at parse time by Query::new in parser.rs; a bad query returns ParserError::QueryError for every PHP parse, so the compile unit test is mandatory.

Every capture-name prefix matters: write., read., writeread. classify def-use sites; call, import_path and type_ref are the only capture names consumed for those features; function, class, func_name, method_name, class_name and type_name drive elements.

The import fallback in parser_elements.rs (line 146) stores the full trimmed node text as the module string, so `use App\Models\User;` is reported with the `use` keyword and semicolon unless a PHP branch is added in parser_elements.rs, which is outside languages/.

tree-sitter-php must be declared in root [workspace.dependencies] and in crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml; the workspace uses tree-sitter 0.27.1 and tree-sitter-language 0.1.9 is already locked, so the grammar's tree-sitter-language 0.1 dependency aligns.

The new Cargo.lock entry must be at least 7 days old for cargo deny package age checks (AGENTS.md). tree-sitter-php v0.25.2 was tagged 2026-11-19, which is 9 days before the run date; the crates.io publish date was not checked.

PHP needs the php dialect (LANGUAGE_PHP), not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY, because only the php dialect's program rule admits the text node for inline HTML (grammar source: program is seq(optional(text), optional(seq(php_tag, repeat(statement)))) when dialect === 'php').

Node text of a variable_name includes the leading `$`, but the captured inner name node does not; defuse matching compares node text to the symbol name, so PHP queries must capture the inner (name) node and callers pass the bare name.
CI runs cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo fmt --check; workspace lints deny unwrap_used and expect_used outside tests.
Commits must be conventional, GPG-signed and signed off (CONTRIBUTING.md). Tags are GPG-signed annotated tags; the release process is out of scope.

supported_languages() in lang.rs is not exhaustive (css and yaml are absent) and mod.rs module docs still mention Cargo lang-* features that were removed. A PHP entry should be added there for consistency, but the stale entries are not in scope.
Issue scope: no tool handler or schema changes; no .phtml, .inc, .module or .php5 extensions; no trait use resolution, property or constant extraction, attributes or namespace alias import handling.

approaches.name: A: Full Java/Swift-pattern handler (recommended)
approaches.description: Add php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class, interface, trait, enum), CALL_QUERY (function, member, nullsafe member, scoped calls), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration as a whole node), DEFUSE_QUERY (assignments, update, parameters, variable reads) and extract_inheritance as a child-kind walk over base_clause and class_interface_clause. Use LANGUAGE_PHP for the php dialect. Wire "php" into get_language_info, get_ts_language, EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages; set extract_function_name, find_method_for_receiver and find_receiver_type to None; add crate deps, lock entry, README and docs list updates; add unit tests in php.rs and an integration test file.
pros: Satisfies every item in the issue's Scope and Acceptance Criteria, including the mixed HTML/PHP zero-ERROR requirement via LANGUAGE_PHP.
Follows the Swift wiring (most recent language) and the Java query shape; no changes outside languages/, lang.rs, Cargo files, README and tests.
DEFUSE_QUERY is included, so analyze_symbol def-use works for PHP variables with the bare-name convention.
Child-kind inheritance walk matches the grammar and does not depend on field names that do not exist.
cons: Import text is the raw use statement via the fallback branch (includes 'use' and ';') unless parser_elements.rs gets a PHP branch.
PHP has no declaration-style local variables; the local write capture has to come from simple_parameter, which is an approximation.
Crate age check requires the 0.25.2 tag to be old enough on crates.io; not verified in this run.
Needs a manual binary size measurement for the PR description.

approaches.name: B: Minimal registry-only handler
approaches.description: Follow the css/yaml pattern: ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY only; reference_query, defuse_query and extract_inheritance set to None; wire the same registry points. Inheritance is dropped or derived from the element query alone.
pros: Smallest diff and fastest path to a green build.
Matches the css and yaml handlers, which already ship without defuse or inheritance.
cons: Violates the issue's Scope, which requires the five query constants and extract_inheritance, and fails the 'extends Bar implements A, B' acceptance criterion.
analyze_symbol def-use returns nothing for PHP; the issue's acceptance criteria do not mention def-use but the Scope does.
Reviewer would reject a partial integration against the stated scope.

approaches.name: C: PHP-only grammar or per-file dialect switch
approaches.description: Use LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for pure .php files and keep LANGUAGE_PHP for mixed files, selecting the dialect per file. Alternatively wire only LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY for a smaller AST without text nodes.
pros: Pure PHP files parse with a simpler tree (no text nodes), so queries are tighter.
Clear separation of pure and template PHP if the project later wants both.
cons: LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY program rule has no text node, so a mixed HTML/PHP file produces ERROR nodes, which violates the acceptance criterion if this dialect is used alone.
A per-file dialect switch needs a second language name or a branch in get_ts_language, which is keyed only by language name; this touches more of the registry than Approach A.
Doubles the test matrix and needs a dialect-detection rule that the issue does not specify.

recommendation: Approach A. It is the only option that satisfies the issue's Scope and all acceptance criteria: it uses LANGUAGE_PHP (required for the mixed-template criterion), includes the DEFUSE_QUERY the scope requires, and follows the Java query shape and the Swift inheritance guard. The main cost is the import fallback text and the single-variable local-write approximation, both of which can be documented in the PR. B is a fallback only if the maintainers narrow scope.

inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: php/grammar.js (a one-line wrapper calling defineGrammar('php')) and common/define-grammar.js (rules at lines 319-332 interface_declaration, 334-337 base_clause, 365-379 class_declaration, 381-383 class_interface_clause), plus php/src/node-types.json. Literal rules: class_declaration: prec.right(seq(optional(field('attributes', $.attribute_list)), repeat($._modifier), keyword('class'), field('name', reserved('classes', $.name)), optional($.base_clause), optional($.class_interface_clause), field('body', $.declaration_list))). base_clause: seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)). class_interface_clause: seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)). _name: choice(alias(keyword('static', false), $.name), alias(choice(...CAST_TYPE_CLASS_NAMES...), $.name), reserved('classes', $.name), $.qualified_name, $.relative_name). node-types.json confirms class_declaration has no field named superclass or interfaces; base_clause and class_interface_clause appear only in its children list, unnamed by field(). Walk, field by field: (1) for i in 0..class.child_count(), take child(i); (2) if child.kind() == "base_clause", iterate its named children; each child whose kind is name, qualified_name or relative_name yields "extends <source text>"; (3) if child.kind() == "class_interface_clause", iterate its named children with the same kind filter and yield "implements <source text>"; (4) every other child, including the keyword tokens class, extends, implements and the body, is skipped. Upstream queries/tags.scm uses the same shape: (class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name). Using child_by_field_name would return None and silently produce [] for PHP, so the Java walk cannot be copied.
